title: So he's coming tomorrow
goal: Pass on what you have found out or heard about an action with eken after -ýAn, -An, -jAk and -mAlY.

intro.text: *eken* after a verb form reports what you found out or heard: *Ol her gün pyýada gidýän eken* (she walks every day, it turns out), *Olar göçen eken* (they've moved), *Myhmanlar ertir geljek eken* (they're coming tomorrow, I hear), *Ol gelmeli eken* (he has to come).

vocab.en: to leave one's job, to quit

exercises.question: How do you say **the guests are coming tomorrow, I hear**?

why.1: *gelen eken* is about what has happened: **they came, it turns out**.

exercises.explain: `-jAk` + *eken*: something that will happen, as you heard.

exercises.label: *gelmek*: I'm coming, it turns out; you're coming…

accept: gelýän ekenim
gelýän ekeniň
gelýän eken

exercises.explain: *gelýän* stays; *eken* takes the past endings with a linking vowel: *ekenim*, *ekeniň*, and nothing for **he, she**.

exercises.text: Olar Mara göç___ eken. Men bilmeýärdim.
exercises.en: They've moved to Mary, it turns out. I didn't know.

accept: en

reject.why: *göçýän eken* would be **they're moving**. For what has happened: *göçen eken*.

exercises.explain: *göç-* + *-en* + *eken*: they've moved, as you found out.

accept: Aýna is getting married, I hear.
Aýna is going to get married, I hear.
I hear Aýna is [getting married|going to get married].
Apparently Aýna is [getting married|going to get married].
Aýna is [getting married|going to get married], apparently.

exercises.prompt: So it was a lie! (You've just found out.)
accept: Bu ýalan eken!
Ol ýalan eken!

reject.why: *ýalandy* only says **it was a lie**. Finding it out: *ýalan eken*.

exercises.explain: *eken* after a noun ([A2 unit 2](a2-u02)): you have just found it out.

exercises.question: Which is **he doesn't eat meat, it turns out**?

why.1: *iýmedik eken*: **he didn't eat** the meat, it turns out (on one occasion).
why.2: *iýmejek eken*: **he won't eat** meat, I hear.

exercises.explain: For what is usually so, `-ýAn`, negative *-mAýAn*: *iýmeýän eken*.

exercises.prompt: Ol her gün işe pyýada gidýän eken.
accept: She walks to work every day, it turns out.
It turns out she walks to work every day.
[He|She] walks to work every day, apparently.
Apparently [he|she] walks to work every day.
He walks to work every day, it turns out.
It turns out he walks to work every day.
[He|She] goes to work on foot every day, it turns out.

exercises.gloss: working (as in “she works, it turns out”: … eken)
exercises.explain: `-ýAn` is like `-ýAr` with *n*: *işle-ýän*, as in *Ol şu ýerde işleýän eken*.

exercises.prompt: Merdan has to come at eight, it seems.
accept: Merdan sagat sekizde gelmeli eken.
Sagat sekizde Merdan gelmeli eken.
exercises.explain: `-mAlY` + *eken*: something that has to happen, as you found out.

exercises.text: Merdan işden çyk___ eken. Indi ol täze iş gözleýär.
exercises.en: Merdan has quit his job, it turns out. Now he's looking for a new job.

accept: an

reject.why: *çykýan eken* would be about what happens regularly. For what has happened: *çykan eken*.

exercises.explain: *çyk-* + *-an* + *eken*: he has left, as you found out.

accept: I was wrong, it turns out.
It turns out I was wrong.
I was mistaken, it turns out.
It turns out I was mistaken.
Apparently I was wrong.
I was wrong, I see.

exercises.prompt: Merjen's family has moved to Ashgabat, it turns out.
accept: Merjeniň maşgalasy Aşgabada göçen eken.
Merjeniň maşgalasy Aşgabada göçüpdir.

reject.why: *göçdi* states it as something you knew or saw. You've found it out: *göçen eken*, or *göçüpdir*.

exercises.explain: *göçen eken* stresses your discovery; *göçüpdir* is the everyday way to pass it on. Both fit.
